title: Constructible sheaves over a finite ring have etale origin
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. For the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] of the small pro-etale and etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and the constructibility notions [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], pullback $\nu_T^*$ induces an equivalence between constructible sheaves of $B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and intrinsically constructible sheaves of $B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (locally constant with finite module stalks on a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes).

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible; global finite-stratification refinement using restriction compatibility and finite locally constant comparison (lemma-compare-locally-constant, Tag 099Y). No qcqs assumption on T is imposed.

proof.text:
Let $G$ be a constructible etale $B$-module sheaf, with its finite global partition $i_k:S_k	o T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], its finite constant values give locally constant restrictions with finite stalks. The isomorphism $i_{k,\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_T^*G\cong
u_{S_k}^*i_{k,\mathrm{Et}}^*G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and clause (a) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] show that each restriction of $
u_T^*G$ is lisse. The same partition, with the same subscheme structures, therefore witnesses intrinsic constructibility. No affine-local-to-global constructibility criterion is used.

proof.text:
Write $F_T=
u_T^*$ and $R_T=
u_{T,*}$. The unit $\eta_G:G	o R_TF_TG$ is invertible for every etale $B$-module sheaf by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. The adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(F_TG,F_TH)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,R_TF_TH)$, and postcomposition with $\eta_H^{-1}$ identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$. Thus $F_T$ is fully faithful on all module sheaves. Call a pro-etale sheaf classical if it is isomorphic to $F_TG$ for some etale sheaf. It is classical exactly when its counit $\epsilon_P:F_TR_TP	o P$ is invertible: one implication takes $G=R_TP$, and the other uses naturality and the triangle identity $\epsilon_{F_TG}\circ F_T\eta_G=1$. In particular fully faithful $F_T$ lifts an isomorphism between two of its images uniquely, together with the inverse. Coefficients: the sheaves of $B_T$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] are the module sheaves over $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] with $\Lambda=B$, used by the theorems cited in steps 3, 4 and 7. Indeed the ring map from the constant presheaf $U\mapsto B$ to $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),B)$ sending $b$ to the constant function is injective for $U
eq\emptyset$; it is locally surjective, because a continuous function to the finite discrete $B$ is constant on the finitely many clopen open subschemes where it takes each value, which cover $U$. Hence both sheafifications agree, compatibly with the constant sections.

Being classical is Zariski-local. For an open immersion $v:V\to T$, restriction of a pro-etale sheaf is evaluation on objects over $V$, by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The explicit direct-image formula in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] consequently gives $(R_TP)|_V=R_V(P|_V)$: both evaluate to $P(W)$ for etale $W\to V$. Together with [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], this identifies $\epsilon_P|_V$ with $\epsilon_{P|_V}$, since the evaluation counit and its adjoint restriction are the same maps. If $P$ is classical on an open cover, these restricted counits are invertible by step 2. The open family is a pro-etale cover: its pullbacks cover each affine object, and quasi-compactness of that object supplies a finite subcover by quasi-compact affine opens. Locality for covering families, clause (1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], then makes $\epsilon_P$ invertible globally. Only covering locality is used, never conservativity of geometric stalks on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, local reduction; comparison counit on open localizations

proof.text: Classical $B$-module sheaves are closed under extensions. For $0\to F_TG'\to P\to F_TG''\to0$, [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] gives a distinguished triangle with boundary $\delta:F_TG''[0]\to F_TG'[0][1]$. Exactness of $F_T$ follows from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] makes its termwise derived functor triangulated. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts $\delta$ to $\varphi:G''[0]\to G'[0][1]$. By TR1 and inverse rotation TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], complete it in the unbounded derived category to a triangle $G'[0]\to H\to G''[0]\xrightarrow{\varphi}G'[0][1]$. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $H^q(H)=0$ for $q\ne0$. Thus [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] identifies $H\cong G[0]$, where $G=H^0(H)$; in particular $H$ is bounded below. The image triangle and the extension triangle have the same boundary $\delta$. Rotate both twice to start with $\delta$; TR3 supplies a triangle morphism with identity first two components. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] the third component is invertible, yielding $F_TH\cong P[0]$. Take $H^0$ to obtain $F_TG\cong P$. Exactness identifies $H^0(F_TG[0])=F_TG$ by preservation of the kernel and image defining cohomology. No constructibility of $G$ has been asserted.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, extension argument; derived full faithfulness and lifting the extension boundary

proof.text: For every $N\geq0$, induct on the assertion that, for every scheme $Y$, a pro-etale $B$-module sheaf $P$ lisse on a finite constructible locally closed partition with at most $N$ nonempty strata is classical. For $N=0$, $Y$ is empty; the empty covering forces its module sheaf to be zero, the pullback of the zero etale sheaf. Assume the assertion for $N-1$. For $y\in Y_k$, [lem-sf-constructible-partition-local-closed-stratum] gives an affine open $V\ni y$ such that $Y_k\cap V$ is closed and $U=V\setminus(Y_k\cap V)$ is quasi-compact. Use the fibre-product subschemes $S_i\times_YV$ and $S_i\times_YU$; they are immersions by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Their images remain locally closed and constructible: the former is preserved by intersection with an open, and for the latter use [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Indeed a retrocompact open restricts to a retrocompact open on any open subspace, because each quasi-compact open of that subspace is also a quasi-compact open of $Y$; restrict the finite unions and differences in the definition. The lisse restrictions remain lisse on these open subschemes of the original strata: restrict their trivializing covers, with the same constant values and the same geometric stalks. Thus $P|_U$ has at most $N-1$ nonempty strata, while $P$ restricted to $Z=S_k\times_YV$ is lisse. The next two steps show $P|_V$ classical; step 3 will then glue these neighbourhoods.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, induction on strata; Tags 09AH, 09AF, 09A6

proof.text: The immersion $i:Z\to V$ just obtained is a closed immersion, even when its stratum scheme structure is nonreduced. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it factors as a closed immersion into an open $W\subset V$. Its image $C=Y_k\cap V$ is closed in $V$, so $W$ and $V\setminus C$ cover $V$. The structure-sheaf map $\mathcal O_V\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective on $W$ by that factorization and on $V\setminus C$ because its target there is zero; hence it is surjective. The underlying map is a homeomorphism onto $C$, giving the claimed closed immersion by the same definition. The complementary inclusion $j:U\to V$ is quasi-compact: on the affine $V$, the quasi-compact open $U$ has a finite cover by principal opens $D(f_a)$, whose intersections with any principal open $D(g)$ are the finitely many affine $D(f_ag)$.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, induction on strata; Tags 09AH, 09AF, 09A6

proof.text:
Induction now gives $j^*P_V\cong
u_U^*G_U$, and clause (b) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] gives $i^*P_V\cong
u_Z^*G_Z$. Apply [lem-sf-proetale-open-closed-sequence], whose quasi-compactness hypothesis was checked in step 6, to obtain $0	o j_!j^*P_V	o P_V	o i_*i^*P_V	o0$. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] its first term is $
u_V^*(j_!G_U)$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] makes $i$ affine; clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $G_Z[0]\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},B)$ and take $H^0$ to identify its last term with $
u_V^*(i_*G_Z)$. For this passage, [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] identifies degree-zero derived direct image with ordinary direct image: the latter preserves kernels as a right adjoint; the source module sheaf categories on our small sites are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Exactness of $
u_V^*$, already cited in step 4, commutes with degree-zero cohomology. Both end terms are therefore classical. Step 4 makes $P_V$ classical; step 3 makes $P$ classical. This completes the induction also when $N=1$ and $U$ is empty, without identifying a surjective stratum immersion with an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, induction on strata; Tags 09AH, 09AF, 09A6

proof.text:
Let $P$ be intrinsically constructible, and choose $G$ with $
u_T^*G\cong P$ by step 7. Retain the original global finite partition $i_k:S_k	o T$ of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $
u_{S_k}^*(i_k^{-1}G)\cong i_k^*P$. Clause (b) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] gives a lisse etale sheaf $H_k$ with $
u_{S_k}^*H_k\cong i_k^*P$. Full faithfulness from step 2, applied on $S_k$, lifts the resulting isomorphism to $i_k^{-1}G\cong H_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], each $H_k$ admits etale local trivializations with finite constant $B$-module values. Thus precisely the original partition witnesses constructibility of $G$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Combined with preservation in step 1 and full faithfulness in step 2, this proves the asserted equivalence. The argument works for arbitrary $T$, the zero finite ring, zero sheaves, and empty strata; it neither replaces $B$ by a valuation-ring quotient nor equates global finite partitions with affine-local constructibility.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 8 use its finite global partition and finite module values to identify precisely the source subcategory; the unit has no alternative definition of this sheaf notion.
Steps 1 and 8 convert finite etale constant module values to finite stalks and back; this finite-ring local-trivialization tool is not stated elsewhere in the unit.
Steps 1, 7, and 8 use clauses (a) and (b) for arbitrary finite commutative rings on strata; the unit comparison nodes do not give locally constant descent.
Step 1 identifies the intrinsic target subcategory through its actual global partition definition; no proper-base-change statement supplies this definition.
Step 3 identifies restriction to an open with evaluation over that open; the comparison adjunction alone does not identify localized pro-etale sites.
Step 3 uses only clause (1), covering locality for a sheaf counit; no geometric-stalk assertion or base-change result of that node is used.
Step 4 associates the boundary distinguished triangle to a short exact sequence in an arbitrary abelian category; this is a generic derived-category tool.
Step 4 applies exact pullback termwise and preserves triangles and shifts; the unit full-faithfulness theorem does not itself state triangle preservation.
Step 4 uses TR1, TR2 and TR3 to complete and compare the lifted boundary triangles; these are the defining generic triangulated-category axioms.
Step 4 deduces the third component is invertible from the two identity components of the rotated triangle morphism; this is a generic triangle tool.
Step 4 proves the lifted extension cone has cohomology only in degree zero; the unit has no generic cohomology-triangle statement.
Step 4 identifies the cone with its degree-zero cohomology sheaf; this generic truncation consequence is not a proper-base-change input.
Step 5 obtains the affine neighbourhood, closed selected stratum and quasi-compact open complement needed for induction; it is a generic constructible-partition tool.
Step 7 uses the open-closed short exact sequence with quasi-compact complementary open and arbitrary finite-ring coefficients; no node of the unit gives this recollement sequence.
Step 7 identifies the open end term as a comparison pullback; this generic open-immersion identity supplies no alternative proper-base-change route.
Step 7 takes degree-zero cohomology of derived direct-image comparison using left exactness and enough injectives; this is the generic right-derived-functor identification.
Step 6 checks an immersion with closed image is a closed immersion from the topological embedding and structure-sheaf surjectivity definition.
Step 7 uses only clause (b), that a closed immersion is affine, to establish hypotheses of the unit direct-image comparison.
Step 7 uses clause (3), affine morphisms are qcqs, to apply the unit direct-image comparison to the selected closed stratum.
Step 7 supplies enough injectives from the unit Grothendieck module-sheaf theorem, so the cited degree-zero resolution lemma applies.
Step 5 uses clause (1), stability of immersions under base change, to restrict the original stratum subschemes to V and U; this is a generic scheme tool, not a replacement proper-base-change route.
Step 5 expands the finite union of differences of retrocompact opens to prove that constructible stratum images restrict to any open subspace.
